text:
priya: Heads up — eu-west2 scratchpool backlog is now blocking GPU warmups, seeing allocation stalls for ~20% of queued jobs. noticed right after the nightly janitor window.
sam: ugh, any iostat or scrub metrics? is it the fsync/scrub overlap again?
priya: putting a quick iostat and janitor summary below:
priya: ```
Device            r/s     w/s     rkB/s     wkB/s  await
nvme0n1         120.4  10234.6   4096.0  327680.0   25.3
``` 
priya: janitor logs show many concurrent scrub workers >12 and lots of small random writes. scrub_inflight_slots metric jumped to 18.
kevin: if scrub concurrency is that high it will saturate IO scheduler and blow out our provisioning headroom for ephemeral launches. :grimacing:
ops-jen: region note — eu-west2 only, other regions look fine. we already have reduced scrub window there historically due to thermal limits.
maria: any signs of actual corruption or just latency/wear spikes? we should avoid aggressive disable unless safe.
priya: no filesystem corruption observed. dmesg shows read_retries and a few "media error" messages on nvme0n1 but no remap yet. log snippet:
priya: ```
[ 3421.123456] nvme0n1: read err status: -84
[ 3421.123457] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 98304
```
sam: hmm that's scary. Could be firmware wearing patterns + heavy scrub IO. What's the immediate mitigation? throttle janitor?
kevin: temp mitigation idea: reduce janitor concurrency from 16 -> 4 on eu-west2 and add aggressive backoff in janitor controller. also bump scrub throttle to honor iops_budget per-device.
priya: I can roll a canary patch to the janitor config: set `scrub.max_workers=4` and `scrub.iops_limit=4000` for eu-west2. command to patch config:
priya: ```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config --patch '{"data":{"scrub.max_workers":"4","scrub.iops_limit":"4000"}}'
``` 
ops-jen: ok but note cost + SLO tradeoff: slower scrub means higher long-term wear risk if backlog persists. ops team prefers staged backoff windows.
maria: +1 to staged approach. Also create an alert for read_retry_rate > 5/min so we can escalate before remap.
eng-sre-bot: auto: created alert `nvme_read_retry_rate_eu_west2` threshold=5/min, severity=page_on_escalation.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary patch queued for 3 hosts in eu-west2, rolling update scheduled in 2m.
priya: canary started. monitoring queue length and GPU warmup success rate. will abort roll if iops > 7000 or read_retry spikes.
kevin: if canary looks good, plan to roll to remaining hosts during low-load window (03:00 UTC). also follow-up plan: add tenant-aware janitor limits so heavy scrubs don't starve GPU allocation.
sam: noted. also let's capture a postmortem brief: TL;DR root cause = scrub concurrency + device retry spike + region thermal cap -> IO queue saturation -> GPU provisioning stall.
priya: creating a short runbook and incident note. will add action items: throttle, alert, firmware check, longer-term: tenant-aware scrub, rewrite janitor backoff.
maria: thanks. ping me if any remap occurs, we'll prioritize disk replacement.
priya: thanks everyone, will update thread after 30m monitoring.
